text:
Last season Dylan Cozens was one of the most quietly valuable forwards in the league: Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.0 wins, 53rd among 401 forwards, with most of it coming from defense, and his chances outran his goals. This season the defensive edge hasn't shown up yet. At five on five, Ottawa has had 46.98% of the expected goals with him on, 7.57 points worse than without him.

The style is intact: fast (speed bursts in the 89th percentile by NHL EDGE), physical with 53 hits, and a rush player, with 53% of his shots coming off the rush in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season. But his own chance rate has dropped from 1.29 expected goals per hour to 0.9, and he's shooting 8.9% against a league norm of 13.3%.

The last ten games have been better, 4 goals and 9 points on 16.9 minutes a night. At 25, with 4 goals and 12 points through 21 games, this is a player whose underlying game earned more trust than his line shows. Watch the defensive numbers first; they were his calling card.
headline: Dylan Cozens is waiting on his process
